Module 2.title: C Fundamentals: Data Types, Operators and Control Structures
Module 2.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: C Basics
  • Data Types & Sizes: char (1 byte), int (4 bytes), float (4 bytes), double (8 bytes).
  • Operators: Arithmetic, Relational, Logical ($&&, ||, !$), Bitwise ($\&, |, \^, \sim, <<, >>$), Ternary ($?:$).
  • Branching: if-else ladder, switch-case (integral expressions only, break statement prevents fallthrough).
  • Loops: Entry-controlled (for, while) vs Exit-controlled (do-while: executes at least once).

Module 3.title: Arrays, Strings and Modular Functions
Module 3.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Arrays & Functions
  • Array Memory: Contiguous memory allocation. 1D: base address $+ i \times \text{size}$. 2D: Row-major order ($base + [i \times N + j] \times size$).
  • Functions: Pass by value (copies actual parameter) vs Pass by reference (passes address using pointers).
  • Recursion: Function calling itself; requires base stopping condition to prevent stack overflow.
  • Strings: Null-terminated character arrays (`'\0'`). Standard functions: `strlen()`, `strcpy()`, `strcat()`, `strcmp()`.
Module 3.detailed_notes:
Module 3 Reference: Modular Functions

Storage classes in C: auto (stack), register (CPU registers), static (persistent across calls), extern (global linkage).
Module 3.textbook_html:

Module 4.title: Pointers and Dynamic Memory Allocation
Module 4.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Pointers
  • Pointer Concept: Variable storing memory address (`int *p = &var;`). Dereferencing: `*p` accesses value.
  • Pointer Arithmetic: `p + 1` increments address by `sizeof(*p)` bytes. Array name acts as constant pointer to first element (`arr == &arr[0]`).
  • Dynamic Memory Functions (stdlib.h):
    • `malloc(n * sizeof(int))`: Allocates uninitialized contiguous heap memory.
    • `calloc(n, sizeof(int))`: Allocates and initializes heap memory to zero.
    • `realloc(ptr, new_size)`: Resizes allocated memory block.
    • `free(ptr)`: Releases heap block, prevents memory leaks.
Module 4.detailed_notes:
Module 4 Reference: Heap Management

Dangling pointers, memory leaks, and pointer-to-pointer structures.
Module 4.textbook_html:

Module 5.title: Structures, Unions and File Input/Output
Module 5.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary: Structures & File I/O
  • Structure (`struct`): User-defined type grouping variables of different data types. Memory size $\ge$ sum of members (due to padding/alignment). Access via dot operator (`s.name`) or arrow (`ptr->name`).
  • Union (`union`): Members share the exact same memory space. Size equals size of largest member.
  • File Operations: `fopen()`, `fclose()`, `fprintf()`, `fscanf()`, `fread()`, `fwrite()`. Modes: `"r"` (read), `"w"` (write/truncate), `"a"` (append), `"rb"/"wb"` (binary).
Module 5.detailed_notes:
Module 5 Reference: File Systems

Sequential vs random file access using `fseek(fp, offset, SEEK_SET)` and `ftell(fp)`.
